board.title: The Vibrating Crystal Inside Every Wristwatch

scenes.narration: Your wristwatch does not keep accurate time using complex mechanical springs. It relies on a microscopic tuning fork hidden inside the movement.
Protected inside a sealed metal can, the quartz resonator isolates the delicate crystal from outside moisture and dust.
Inside, metal electrodes pass electric signals through the crystal. The piezoelectric effect makes the prongs vibrate thirty-two thousand seven hundred and sixty-eight times a second.
scenes.label: 32,768 HZ

scenes.narration: Micro-electronic circuits divide that high frequency fifteen times, outputting one pulse per second to turn a small gear meshed with a larger gear.
scenes.label: 2^15 DIVIDER

scenes.narration: A tiny battery supplies continuous energy, allowing the motor coil to advance the clock hand precisely once every second.
